label: doc_title
text: LOCAL AND GENERAL.

label: text
text: Singapore's contribution to the St. Paul's Cathedral Restoration Fund totals $24,397.98.

label: text
text: "Stated to have motored at 35 miles an hour, Richard Leslie Friday, of Walthamstow, did not appear at West Ham, but sent a blank cheque. He was fined £5."

label: text
text: A human dynamo is the name applied to Johnny Hines, the screen comedian. The reason is seen in his acting, especially that in “Little Johnny,” at the World Theatre showing for two more days only.

label: text
text: The Hongkong Angling Club announces a Salt Water Competition in May under conditions which have been notified to members. Members are asked to notify the Hon. Secretary, Mr. E. B. C. Hornell if they desire to participate in the competition.

label: text
text: As from to-day, the “Overland China Mail” (weekly summary) of the “China Mail”) will be ready every Friday morning so that subscribers will have ample time to catch the mail for Home. Applications for copies should be made to the office of the publishers (“China Mail” building).

label: text
text:
Fishing off Sydney Heads recently I picked up a beer bottle containing a note. It read: "The person who finds this bottle will also find that the beer is gone. Lightning plays some queer pranks. A few years ago, a young girl was sitting indoors at Moonan Flat when a flash of lightning burnt the hair off her head, passed down both sides of the body, skipped the corsets and, passing down each leg, tore both boots off, sending them yards away. Prior to this the girl was delicate, but she improved wonderfully after her experience.
The annual ordinary general of Messrs. Lane Crawford Ltd., is to be held on Wednesday the 29th inst.

label: text
text: The hearing of the injunction by the Pacific Mail Steamship Co., against the sale by the U.S. Shipping Board of the five Trans-Pacific steamers at present operated by the Pacific Mail Company, has been postponed until April 20.

label: text
text: A treaty of extradition has been signed by Rumania and the United States which provides that Rumania is not now compelled to extradite persons who would suffer capital punishment in America. In Rumania capital punishment is illegal.

label: text
text: One case of small pox; one of diphtheria and one of enteric fever (all Chinese—small pox case imported) were notified for the 24 hours ended Tuesday last.

label: text
text: Two septuagenarian all-the-year-round bathers were present at the St. Pancras Swimming Club's annual dinner—Mr. G. Webster, the president, aged 77, who won a race last Christmas in Hampstead Ponds, and Mr. R. Ledger, aged 73, of the Serpentine Swimming Club.

label: text
text: Employment throughout Canada showed considerable recovery during February from the losses at the beginning of January, as indicated by reports of employers on February 1, Statements from 5,832 firms, employing 709,878 persons, show an increase of 16,821 more than on January 1, 1925. Improvement in manufacturing was most pronounced, while logging and construction also afforded largely increased employment. Mining and trade, however, showed contractions. Activity in all, except the Prairie Provinces, increased considerably, but the revival in Quebec was not marked.

label: text
text: Sir Alfred Dent, K. C. M. G., has resigned his seat on the Board of Directors of the Chartered Bank of India, Australia and China owing to ill-health, and Mr. Archibald Audjo Jamieson of the Borneo Co., Ltd., has been elected to fill the vacancy.

label: text
text: Mr. S. Kawashima, who has been appointed Consul-General to Hamburg, is a passenger on the s.s. Kushima Maru.

label: text
text: Mr. and Mrs. U'Gorman Anderson left for Shanghai by the s.s. President Jackson yesterday. Mr. Anderson is now on the staff of the Customs at Shanghai. Mrs. Anderson (Stella Benson) will later leave for Home via America.

label: text
text: Two boys were charged at Highgate with breaking into a tennis pavilion. Magistrate: Did you go to play tennis? One boy: No; to play truant.

label: text
text: Introduced as a “distinguished visitor” to a gathering of Leicestershire children, the Bishop of Peterborough asked them to identify him. “You are the Pope,” was the answer.

label: text
text: The film, The Epic of Everest is only booked for 50 of 4,000 cinemas in Great Britain. The Daily Express scathingly comments on the fact that a wonderful picture dealing with the real heroism and real adventure apparently does not appeal to theatre managers because it contains no love interest and makes no sex appeal. This film will be shown in Hongkong.

label: text
text: Members of St. George's Society are reminded of the tiffin to be held in the Hongkong Hotel on Thursday next.

label: text
text: The Rev. A. D. Stewart will conduct a series of Bible Studies at the Feleno May Institute on Friday Morning. The First will be on Friday 17, at 10.80 a.m. The meeting is open to all women.

label: doc_title
text: SOCIAL AND PERSONAL.

label: text
text:
Mr. J. T. Easterbrook and Mr. F. C. Douglas returned to the Colony by the Mishima Maru yesterday.
The Edinburgh Savings Bank funds show an increase in 1924, compared with the previous year, of £48,780. There was a steady progress in the business of the bank, and the total amount deposited in all departments is now just under £9,500,000. Over 11,000 new accounts were opened during the past year. At the annual meeting of the bank Mr. Sleigh, the Lord Provost, spoke of the appeal the savings bank made to the small investor, and pointed out that, of the amount deposited during the year, 68 per cent of the sums were under £5. Lord Sands, one of the Scottish judges, said it was estimated that practically every second person in Edinburgh was a small investor.

label: text
text: Major R. S. S. Paton has become President of the Garrison Recreation Club.

label: text
text: The Rev. Father Tlaczek is now the officiating clergyman to the Roman Catholic troops in Hongkong.

label: text
text: Mr. William Evans, of Tyncelyn, Llanfrothen; Merioneth, who is in his 75th year, has retired, after serving over 40 years as houndsman with the Ynysfor Hounds. He took part in 500 fox and otter hunts.

label: text
text: Captain J. Macready, D.S.O., who is D.A.A. and Q.M.G. of the China Command, has been promoted to the rank of Major. Major Macready is a grandson of "the great Macready," who in his day was perhaps England's greatest tragedy, and is himself an amateur actor of very high attainments.

label: text
text: Mr. Max Malini, the magician, who entertained a number of parties in Tokio and Yokohama, on his recent trip to Japan, has conjured up a total of Y.420 for the Yokohama General Hospital by a benefit entertainment on board the President Lincoln. The purser took that amount to Tokio when the President Lincoln returned from the United States.

label: text
text: Mr. and Mrs. R. E. O. Bird leave the Colony on retirement on Tuesday next. Mr. Bird is well known as headmaster of the Government's Ellis Kadoorie School, and as a cricketer—particularly as a bowler—of considerable note. Before her marriage, Mrs. Bird, as Miss Clarke was head of the Bellies Girls' School. Both are assured of the best wishes of the community in their retirement from active participation in the life of the Colony.

label: text
text:
Reuter cables the death of John Sergeant the eminent artist; one of the most eminent portrait painters of his day, who was born in 1850 at Florence. He received his education in Italy and in France and studied under Carolus Duran. He first exhibited at the Paris Salon in 1897 and since that date has continuously exhibited there and at the Royal Academy, he was elected an A.R.A. and later was made full Academician. Prior to the war he was the most fashionable as well as one of the greatest and most during portrait painters. His principal works are El Jaleo and the portraits of Duran, Ellen Terry, Joseph Chamberlain, Mr. Carl Meyer and children, Octavin Hill, Lady Faudel Phillips. He will be remembered as the painter also of a war picture which aroused wide comment at the time it was hung at the Royal Academy. Gassed.

label: text
text: Lt. Osborne Woods is reported to have delivered himself of the following:

label: text
text: "Money earned by hard work is not only honestly earned, but not easily spent. I feel that if I buckle down to work, I not only will get back some of the money I have squandered, but will regain the respect of my friends which indeed is more than money can buy."

label: text
text: Mr. F.E. Weatherly who married a second time at 74, and now takes silk at 76, has been described as the most prolific English song writer of the day, and once confessed that he did not know how many he had written, as a curious superstition kept him from ever counting them. But two years ago he told a newspaper representative that the actual number was well over 2,000. His "Nancy Lee" was the effort of but a few minutes and other songs which are very popular are "Nirvana," "The Deathless Army" "Darby and Joan," "We've Come Up From Somerset," "Roses of Picardy," "Thora," and the "Star of Bethlehem."

label: text
text: Funeral services for Miss Burleigh, who was shot and killed in a motor car, were held at the Cathedral of St. Mary and St. John, Manila, the Rev. John P. Williamson, reading the brief service, assisted by Chaplain I. L. Dennett, U. S. A., of Sternberg Hospital. The services were attended by a host of friends of the murdered girl. Captain A. Pickens of Fort McKinley and Mrs. R. F. Carter, also of Fort McKinley, were heard in a duet, with Mrs. Schuyler at the organ. The pall-bearers were Mr. Jack Byron, Lieutenant J. K. Bush, Lieutenant G. H. Carmouche, Lieutenant A. S. Rush, Lieutenant C. F. Beattie and Mr. Jean Cleaver.

label: text
text: E. E. White, better known to his many friends as “Blanco”, has left Manila en route to his home in Canada where he will join his aged mother and remain with her, having retired from the great financial institution, The Sun Life of Canada, which he has served well for twenty seven years as the general representative in the Philippines and Borneo. Probably no other man has played so prominent a part in the development of golf in islands as has “Blanco” White had come, to Manila during the stirring days of ninety eight when the Americans were pouring troops into the Philippines to put down what had developed into an insurrection and already was an enthusiastic golfer. Almost immediately with the help of prominent Britishers and Americans he began to lay plans for a golf course.
